Donald Trump has threatened to strike Iran's power plants and bridges, saying they 'have to pay the price' for taking too long to negotiate.

Earlier, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it has attacked the US navy's Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain with drones after a series of American strikes on cities along the Strait of Hormuz.

Look back on our coverage of events as they unfolded.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:53am

By Thomas Morgan

Donald Trump has been talking to reporters from the Oval Office.

After being asked about the Iran war, the US president once again urges Iran to sign a deal to end the fighting.

And he adds that in addition to the strikes on Tuesday, he says "we'll hit them again today".

He adds that he "can" strike Iranian power plants and infrastructure, but refuses to say whether he will make good on his repeated threat to do so.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:08am

By Daniela Pizzirani

Airlines are gradually restoring some flights to the Middle East as regional carriers rebuild schedules after war-related disruption.

Many carriers outside the Middle East are still diverting Europe-Asia flights to avoid the region.

Qantas, Australia's flag carrier, is adding flights to Rome and Paris to meet an upswing in demand for European routes.

Flights to Paris will increase to five return flights per week from three and the Perth-Singapore service will increase from daily to 10 a week.

Here's a look at the latest from other airlines:

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 12:49am

By Claire Campbell

Qatari negotiators have travelled to Tehran in a bid to finalise a peace agreement between the US and Iran.

The diplomatic effort comes as talks between the warring sides appear to have stalled with the US and Iran exchanging fire following the downing of an American helicopter.

Qatar's delegation is believed to have landed in Tehran after consultation with the US.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 11:53pm

By Claire Campbell

Jennifer Parker, from the University of Western Australia's Defence and Security Institute, says Iran's attack on the US Apache helicopter was a significant ceasefire breach and had "the potential" to put negotiations for a peace deal on the backfoot.

She told ABC's The World the US retaliatory strikes were "largely expected" but it was not yet clear whether it would lead to a further escalation in the war.

"It is important for the US to demonstrate as well that they are still willing to use military force if Iran doesn't comply with either the ceasefire or any future peace deal," the adjunct professor said.

"It's very clear that both sides do want some degree of deal.

"Whether this will escalate into something further isn't clear right now and I think we'll know in the coming days."

She said this flare-up of hostilities was "different" to other ceasefire violations.

"It's showing that Iran is feeling emboldened right now at this stage of both the conflict and negotiations," she said.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 11:40pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

The UN human rights office will deploy a team of investigators to Lebanon next week to assess potential violations of international law.

Lebanon was drawn into the wider Middle East conflict in March when the Tehran-backed Hezbollah militia fired rockets at Israel in solidarity with Iran.

"It's the first time that we are sending this assessment mission, and the idea is indeed to look at violations by all parties — violations of international law, violations of international human rights law, and to document this, and eventually to report back to you on our findings," UN human rights chief Volker Türk said.

More than 3,600 people have been killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon and more than one million Lebanese are displaced.

The crisis is rapidly eroding food security, with nearly one in four people in Lebanon — about 1.24 million people — expected to face crisis and emergency levels of ⁠food insecurity until August, according to the UN.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 11:27pm

By Claire Campbell

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) says it has detained two people who approached troops in southern Lebanon and taken them to Israel for questioning.

"Earlier today, IDF soldiers identified two suspected individuals who approached the area in which IDF soldiers are operating in southern Lebanon," the military said in a statement.

"Following the identification and in order to rule out any threat, the soldiers apprehended the suspected individuals, who were transferred to Israeli territory for further questioning."

Meanwhile, the IDF has issued several evacuation warnings today urging people in three southern Lebanese towns to flee their homes ahead of strikes.

Reporting with AFP

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 11:09pm

By Middle East correspondent Matthew Doran

Donald Trump has certainly begun ratcheting up his rhetoric about Iran in the last few hours.

And, being a man who is both the US President and inherently unpredictable, his words do matter immensely.

But we do need to take his threats of a return to heavy strikes on Iran with a healthy dose of scepticism - in part because of the questionable political appetite in the US for the fighting to resume with Iran, and in part because of how frequently his public declarations have amounted to very little in this war.

I think we've lost count how many times he has said a deal with Iran to end the war in the Middle East was just days away, or was almost finalised, or was imminent because of how desperate Tehran was to strike an agreement.

We're now 103 days since the war began, and 64 days since the ceasefire between the US and Iran was announced to allow those talks to continue in earnest.

And there's been no deal.

That ceasefire was due to last a few weeks. The deadline came and went, and no new firm expiry date was set.

President Trump was widely condemned in early April, when he posted on social media "a whole civilization will die tonight" ahead of that ceasefire being declared.

And, because that truce was announced, he didn't wipe out the entire Iranian civilisation.

Days earlier, he had been threatening to bomb key Iranian infrastructure - bridges and power plants the focus there, as well as desalination plants at one point too.

Some strikes were recorded, including on a bridge still under construction, but nothing was seen on the scale being suggested by the social media posts.

The President has also continued to insist Israel's Prime Minister does as he tells him - but Benjamin Netanyahu then went and attacked Iran, after continuing attacks on parts of Lebanon seemingly in defiance of Trump.

None of this is to say that the US President's current threats, that he "may" order new strikes on bridges and power plants because Iran is taking too long to agree to a deal, are hollow.

But it does provide context as to how this cycle of commentary plays out.

The strikes overnight here in the Middle East have certainly fuelled a lot of concern in the region about what's coming next, particularly after the first direct attacks between Israel and Iran earlier in the week.

And people will be reading the President's remarks with interest and anxiety.

Key Event

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 10:44pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has clapped back at Türkiye after it's president criticised Israel's attacks on Syria and Lebanon.

"The antisemitic dictator Erdoğan — who is committing genocide against the Kurds, supports the Hamas terrorist organization, oppresses his own people and imprisons political rivals — is the last person who can lecture the State of Israel on morality," he wrote on X.

"The State of Israel and the IDF, the most moral army in the world, will continue to take forceful action against Iran and its proxies, which threaten the Middle East and the entire world."

Earlier, the Turkish PM Tayyip Erdogan said that Israel's attacks on Syria and Lebanon had reached a point where they also threaten Turkey.

The president also said there were initiatives, led by Israel, to destabilise the Mediterranean region.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 10:26pm

By Claire Campbell

President Donald Trump has claimed "nothing" was getting through his naval blockade of the Iranian coast, despite analysts believing some Iranian tankers are likely slipping through the blockade.

In April, US forces announced they would intercept or turn back vessels travelling to or from Iran's ports.

"The Fake News Media refuses to report how EFFECTIVE the U.S. Naval BLOCKADE is, the most successful Blockade in the history of Naval Warfare," he wrote on social media.

"NOTHING GETS THROUGH unless we want it to.

"IT IS A STEEL WALL!"

Trump went on to say that "lots of oil" was getting out and Iran was doing zero business "not paying their military, or any of their bills, and quickly becoming a FAILED NATION".

In recent days, marine traffic observers have revealed hundreds of commercial ships have crossed out of the Strait of Hormuz, often by taking "dark" journeys through Iran's "tollbooth route" or with the guidance of the United States.

Analysts believe some Iranian tankers are likely slipping past the US blockade in the opposite direction and entering Iranian waters to be used to store oil offshore.

Key Event

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 9:50pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Following on from President Donald Trump's Truth Social post, the US president also gave a phone interview to Fox News where he again threatened to strike Iran's power plants and bridges.

During the interview, Trump said he may order the new strikes because Tehran is taking too long to make a deal.

In a post on his Truth social media account, Trump said Iran "will have to pay the price" for the delay.

Key Event

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 9:31pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

US President Donald Trump says Iran will "have to pay the price" for taking too long to negotiate a deal.

In a post on his social media account Truth, Trump wrote:

"Iran is all talk and no action," he said.

"They've taken too long to negotiate a deal that would have been great for them, now they will have to pay the price!!"

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 9:15pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Pictures of an Israeli strike in Houmine El Faouqa, a town in southern Lebanon, are coming through from today.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) issued several warnings earlier today urging people in three southern Lebanese towns to flee their homes ahead of strikes.

The forced evacuation orders warned residents to stay away from the towns.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 8:59pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

If you're just joining our coverage, here's what's happened today.

Stay with us as we bring you the latest on what's unfolding in the region.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 8:43pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan says that Israel's attacks on Syria and Lebanon have reached a point where they also threaten Türkiye.

Speaking in parliament, he said Israel's "aggression" posed a threat to the whole world and must be stopped.

The president also said there were initiatives, led by Israel, to destabilise the Mediterranean region.

He warned that "nobody should chase adventures" or join Israel's "boat of mischief".

Moves violating the rights of Turks and Turkish Cypriots would be met with a clear and strong response, he said.

Key Event

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 8:16pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Two crew members are missing after a fire started in the engine room of a tanker off the coast of Oman.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO), without giving further details, reported one casualty.

The UKMTO did not report the cause of the fire.

The alert came just hours after another maritime security incident in the region.

Earlier, a cargo vessel south of Yemen was approached by a boat with six armed people on board.

The UKMTO reported "an exchange of fire" before the small craft was turned away.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 7:53pm

By Daniela Pizzirani

Earlier, we reported explosions heard in the Qeshm city area, according to state media.

Since then, the governor of Qeshm said in a statement that no explosion had occurred on the island.

He also said that the blast sound heard in the area did not originate there.

The report by the Mehr News Agency, which cited local sources,  said the cause of the explosion on Qeshm island could be related to the situation in the Strait of Hormuz.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 7:16pm

By Lewis Wiseman

Iran's Foreign Ministry says diplomatic efforts with the US cannot advance under repeated ceasefire violations.

In a statement, spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said the US was undermining diplomacy through contradictory messages, shifting positions and repeated ceasefire violations.

"Following overnight events, we need to re-assess [the diplomatic path with Washington] … any diplomatic process requires a minimum stable environment," he said.

He added Israel was also damaging the process through repeated ceasefire breaches in Lebanon.

Wed 10 Jun 2026 at 6:47pm

By Lewis Wiseman

China says it is "deeply concerned" over the conflict in the Middle East and has urged against escalation after the US carried out strikes on Iran over the downing of a US helicopter.

"Various relevant parties should maintain calm and exercise restraint, stop intensifying the conflict and escalating the situation, take concrete measures to ease and cool down tensions," Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian told a news briefing.

Russia urged "restraint" in the Iran war after the recent escalation.

"We are extremely concerned about the new round of US-Iranian armed confrontation, which began with the unprovoked US-Israeli aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran," Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told reporters.

"We call on both sides to exercise restraint and to immediately cease military attacks."
